summary: 5. In terms of the above directions, the IA 2/2025 (in Petition No.45/GT/2016) was listed and heard along with IA Nos. 3/2025 and 4/2025, filed in the respective petitions, as stated above. During the hearing, the learned counsel for the Petitioner submitted that though the Commission had reserved its order in Petition Nos. 243/GT/2017 and 409/GT/2020, the same has been listed, keeping in view that the APTEL judgment dated 19.11.2024 relating to Petition No.45/GT/2016, will also have a consequential impact in these petitions. The learned counsel also pointed out that the Petitioner has filed a compilation, referring to the pleadings in Petition No. 45/GT/2016 and the issues raised /allowed by APTEL in the said appeal. Since none was present on behalf of the Respondents, the Commission directed the issuance of notice to the Respondents/ Objectors, to enable them to file their replies/responses in these matters. 6. The Commission, after hearing the parties, adjourned the hearing of these petitions after granting time to the Respondent APDCL to file its reply and the Objector to file his response (along with an affidavit containing certain additional information). The parties were also directed to complete their pleadings in the matter. The objectors - (h) As per clause 8.0 of the PPA dated 30.5.2007 entered between the Petitioner and the Respondent APDCL (previously ASEB), any party claiming “ _force_ companies. The primary objective of this was to protect the rights and interests of the consumers and the public at large. The objector has no past relation with the Petitioner prior to the filing of this petition and is inviting the public to participate in the petition as per the law. (m) The Petitioner did not comply with the terms and conditions of the PPA while the force majeure conditions occurred. They did not communicate to the erstwhile ASEB and the subsequent entities about the occurrence of such force majeure events. Therefore, no time and cost overruns are admissible to the Petitioner. - (e) The objector is only criticizing the judgment, and it is not clear as to how such submissions can even be entertained at this stage. The matter has been remanded back by APTEL, specifically setting aside the findings arrived at by this Commission on the issue of time overrun related to violence and bandhs and a change in the course of the Champamati river. To argue that the Petitioner misled the APTEL by not filing its tariff petition is factually incorrect, as the entire pleadings before this Commission (in Petition No.45/GT/2016) were filed before the APTEL as part of its rejoinder and available, while adjudicating the issues. In any case, all such submissions are beyond the scope of remand, and the objector cannot expand the scope of these proceedings by adding documents at this stage. Objector had not filed any appeal against the order dated 22.5.2017 and cannot claim that APTEL has varied the order in its favour while deciding the appeal filed by the Petitioner. - (f) The objector is seeking to reargue the original tariff petitions by quoting some selective dates. After considering these objections, the Commission had already passed an order dated 22.5.2017, which the Petitioner challenged. The objector had made similar submissions before the APTEL, which had not found favour with it. If the APTEL judgment aggrieves the Objector, it has to file a second appeal, but cannot obliviate the issues which has been decided in the Petitioner’s favour. 22. Reverting back, it is evident that APTEL vide its judgment, has remanded the matter to this Commission, only to decide the issues (a) and (b) afresh and consequently (d), after hearing the parties, and in the light of a whole bunch of documents already filed by the Petitioner. However, we notice that the Respondent APDCL and the Objectors, have attempted to expand the scope of the present remand proceedings, by alleging that the (i) written notice of the occurrence of the force majeure event was not given to the other party by the Petitioner (ii) Petitioner had concealed before this Commission the actual reason for time and cost overrun, as the project was actually delayed due to failure of the contactors (M/s SPML Infra and M/s Punj Lloyd) engaged in civil works package; and (iii) Petitioner had not filed tariff petition before this Commission as per the regulations, and those submitted was with manipulations to get a higher tariff, thereby seeking to reopen the entire issue of time overrun, decided in the order dated 22.5.2017, treating it as an ‘open remand’. 25. We have considered the submissions. APTEL, in its judgment (as quoted in para 15 above), has observed that the Commission, while condoning the delay of only 32 days, has ignored the entire set of documents filed by the Petitioner in support of its claim for condonation of delay for the period April 2013 to January 2015 on account of violence and bandhs. Pursuant to this, the documents filed by the Petitioner in the original tariff petition, (compilation from Page nos. 887-963 of the consolidated pleadings), summarizing all the documents, as stated below, have been examined.
